📣 Digital gold market could reach $170 billion by 2031, WGC and BCG say

🔔 The digital gold market is expected to grow to $160 billion to $170 billion by 2031, and new research suggests that the demand could be as high as $700 billion once there are no more obstacles to adoption. The World Gold Council (WGC) and Boston Consulting Group (BCG) valued the digital gold market at $45–55 billion, which consists of tokenized gold and digital products secured by vaulted gold bullion. In its base case projections it projects growth of approximately 27% annually over the next five years.

🔗 However, the $700 billion figure represents a separate estimate of potential demand if existing barriers to adoption were removed. It is not a forecast of purchases by 2031, as the researchers clarify in their methodology. The report models a faster-growth outcome in which digital gold reaches $270–280 billion by 2031. The higher estimate assumes that restrictions involving investor confidence, distribution, product usefulness and pricing are addressed more quickly.

🌐 Researchers examined more than 70 digital gold products and surveyed over 12,000 retail investors across 12 markets. They conducted interviews with 20 industry experts, including representatives of banks, exchanges, asset managers and gold infrastructure providers. The market projections cover 96 countries representing 98% of global investable wealth. Their calculations combine the number of potential investors, average investable wealth, expected participation and portfolio allocations.
